en: The Chapter on Non-Proliferation, Concerning the Question on Inference.
9. The Question on the Sun’s Heat “Venerable Nāgasena, does this sun burn fiercely at all times, or does it burn feebly at some times?
“Great King, the sun burns fiercely at all times; it does not burn feebly at any time.”
“If, venerable Nāgasena, the sun always burns fiercely, why then does the sun at times burn fiercely and at other times burn feebly?

“There are, great king, four ailments of the sun; oppressed by one or another of these ailments, the sun burns feebly. What are the four? 1. When the sun is afflicted by the ailment of ‘clouds,’ it burns feebly. 2. When the sun is afflicted by the ailment of ‘dust,’ it burns feebly. 3. When the sun is afflicted by the ailment of ‘smoke,’ it burns feebly. 4. When the sun is afflicted by the ailment of ‘eclipse,’ it burns feebly.”
Haze, great king, is a disease of the sun; oppressed by that disease, the sun shines feebly.
Fog, great king, is a disease of the sun; oppressed by that disease, the sun shines feebly.
Cloud, great king, is a disease of the sun; oppressed by that disease, the sun shines feebly.
“Rāhu, Great King, is a disease of the sun; oppressed by that disease, the sun shines feebly.
These, Great King, are the four diseases of the sun, by any one of which the sun, being oppressed, shines feebly.
“It is wonderful, venerable Nāgasena! It is marvelous, venerable Nāgasena! Even for the sun, so endowed with fiery power...”
“Disease will arise even for you; how much more so for other beings? There is no distinction, venerable sir, between one person and another, except for a wise one such as yourself.
Thus ends the ninth discourse, the Question on the Sun’s Heat.
